authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
reachability: Declaration only: `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:5) has no body here. It is called once, in vote at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:412), against the proposal's stored `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:412), and a zero result reverts `NoVotingPower` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:413). The callee is the immutable set at `mifrens` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:322), so a deployment that wires a contract without this selector makes every vote revert (DERIVED).

authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
reachability: Declaration only: `getVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:6) has no body here. authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
reachability: Declaration only: `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:15) has no body here. It is the quorum denominator, called once at `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735) inside the pass test, measured at the proposal's `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735) and scaled by `QUORUM_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735). Every path that decides an outcome runs through it: `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:483) in execute, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:600) in the winner scan, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:611) and the public `passing` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:745), so a reverting or missing implementation blocks execution entirely.

authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable registry address)
reachability: Declaration only: `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:19) has no body here. It is called twice on the immutable `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:323): once when a rotation target is named at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:369) and again when the envelope is installed at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:494), both reverting QuoteNotAllowed. authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the guardian-set quoteOracle address)
reachability: Declaration only: `usdPerRawUnit` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:24) has no body here. It is called once, at `usdPerRawUnit` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:786), and only when the target is non-native and an oracle is wired; a zero price reverts `QuoteNotPriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:786). The address is the mutable `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:784), which the guardian may repoint at any contract via `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:791), so this call is to an address an admin controls (DERIVED).

Unrestricted pure helper with no storage access and no caller inside this file; it exists for user interfaces that must translate a spend budget into the share of the position it converts. Both arguments are caller-supplied, so the loop trip count `n` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:268) is spendBps divided by sliceBps and is bounded only by the uint16 range — up to 65535 iterations when `sliceBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:268) is 1, which is a caller-paid cost in a view call (DERIVED). Each step multiplies before dividing at `rem` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:272), truncating toward zero, so the remaining share rounds DOWN and the reported conversion at `rem` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:274) rounds UP (DERIVED).

Runs once at deployment and is the only writer of every timing parameter. Zero arguments fall back to the mainnet defaults at `MAINNET_VOTING` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:328) and its three siblings; unless `testnet` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:333) is passed, the one-day floors at `MIN_VOTING` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:334), `MIN_COOLDOWN` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:335) and `MIN_EXEC_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:336) apply, and in BOTH modes a lifetime shorter than the execution window reverts `BadTiming` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:341). No floor exists on `ENVELOPE_LIFETIME` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:344) itself beyond that coherence test, and neither `mifrens` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:322) nor `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:323) nor `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:324) is checked for zero or for code, so a mis-wired deployment is only detectable later: a zero guardian dead-ends `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:516), `setGuardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:523) and `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:791) forever (DERIVED).

authority: voter/holder (live MiFrens voting power of at least PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD)
reachability: Open to any holder whose LIVE power clears `PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:365) — five MiFrens — with no deposit and no per-address cap, so proposal ids grow permissionlessly. The budget must be non-zero and at most `MAX_ENVELOPE_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:366), the destination must be on the registry allowlist `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:369) and priceable `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:370). Two envelope-level gates follow: a live, unexpired envelope reverts `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:386) and a recent one reverts `CooldownActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:387), which is why exhausting an envelope clears `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:718). Voting power is frozen at `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:396), the current block, and the window closes at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:393); several proposals may be open simultaneously and are resolved by `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:558).
observations: comment `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:362) says a proposal occupies the only active slot for three days; code `envelope` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:386) refuses only while an ENVELOPE is live and `proposalCount` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:389) increments without limit, so any number of proposals can be open at once.

authority: voter/holder (one ballot per address per proposal, weight from the proposal's snapshot block)
reachability: Permissionless per holder. A nonexistent id reverts `UnknownProposal` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:408), a closed window reverts `VotingClosed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:409) and a repeat ballot reverts `AlreadyVoted` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:410); weight is checkpointed at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:412), so tokens bought after the proposal opened carry none. Ballots are one-way: `hasVoted` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:415) is set before the tally moves and there is no un-vote. This is the only writer of the leader hint, in five branches: growth of the incumbent at `_leadVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:428), first-ever support at `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:432), overtaking at `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:440), retirement of a hint that is `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:443) and older than one full lifetime at `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:460), and dating an untracked live rival at `_openVotedAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:466). Against-votes never touch the hint, which is consistent with `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:558) ranking on FOR-votes alone.

authority: anyone (permissionless once the proposal has closed, passed, and is the winner)
reachability: No caller gate at all — anyone may install a mandate the guild approved. State gates, in order: the id must exist `UnknownProposal` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:480), the vote must have closed `VotingOpen` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:481), it must be neither executed nor cancelled `AlreadyExecuted` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:482), it must clear quorum and the against-tally `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:483), it must BE the leader `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:488), it must be inside `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:491) of its close, and both the allowlist `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:494) and the price feed `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:498) are re-checked against current state. The write is a wholesale struct replacement at `envelope` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:501), so both spend counters restart at `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:504) and `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:507) even if a previous envelope was still live, and `lastEnvelopeAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:509) starts the cooldown that blocks the next proposal. Downstream this is what the registry's rotation path reads through allowance (DERIVED).

Only the address in `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:517) reaches this; everyone else reverts NotGuardian. It accepts ANY id, including one never proposed and one whose vote is still open, and writes `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:518) unconditionally; a later proposal that draws that id overwrites the whole struct at `proposals` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:390), so a pre-marked slot does not persist (DERIVED). The live envelope is only stood down when the cancelled proposal is the one that installed it, via the `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:519) test, and `lastEnvelopeAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:509) is NOT rewound, so the cooldown from the cancelled envelope still runs against the next `propose` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:364) (DERIVED). The guardian can stop but cannot start or redirect a rotation: no path here writes `quote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:502) or `maxTotalBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:503).

Self-rotating role: only the current `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:524) may name the next one at `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:525), with no zero-check, no two-step handover and no event. Passing address zero renounces the role permanently and dead-ends `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:516), `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:791) and this setter, since no transaction can originate from address zero (DERIVED). Nothing else in the contract can restore it — the constructor at `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:324) is the only other writer.

Public view and the selector `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:488) that execute gates on, so it sits on the only path that installs an envelope. Fast path: the hint `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:562) is returned when `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:563) accepts it. Otherwise it walks ids downward from `proposalCount` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:566) and stops at the first proposal whose window closed more than `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:597) ago, so the scan spans only proposals from the last voting period plus execution window; within that span the number of proposals is unbounded and grows with permissionless filing (DERIVED). Ranking is on FOR-votes alone at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:601) with a strict comparison, so a tie keeps the LOWER id encountered last in the downward walk, and a zero return means no proposal is currently executable.
observations: comment `execute` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:538) cites the gate at line 273 and comment `MAX_WINNER_SCAN` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:550) describes a positional bound; code `execute` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:478) is declared far from that line and the loop is bounded instead by the time test at `break` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:597), with no such constant declared.

reachability: Private; the single call site is the fast path in `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:563). It is the one definition of executability: unknown, executed or cancelled proposals fail at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:608), a still-open vote fails at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:609), a stale one fails at `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:610), and the remainder must clear `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:611). Because it is a superset of the scan's own tests, trusting the hint can only elect a proposal the scan would also accept, though not necessarily the highest-voted one unless the hint is maintained as a maximum (DERIVED).

Private; reached only from the hint-retirement branch at `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:443). It is monotone: `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:627) and `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:627) are one-way flags and the deadline at `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:628) only recedes, so a true answer can never become false. An id that was never proposed reads dead because `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:628) is zero (DERIVED).

authority: anyone (the registry rotation path is the production caller)
reachability: Unrestricted view, and the contract's main outward-facing surface: the registry's rotation facet reads it at `allowance` (RedemptionExt.sol:303) and refuses to rotate when the remainder is zero. Three no-envelope cases collapse to the same answer — inactive or expired at `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:645) and exhausted at `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:646) — so the REMAINDER is the liveness flag while `quote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:647) cannot be, address zero being a legitimate native destination. The remainder is a bps budget, not an asset amount, and it is also consumed internally by `allowance` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:700).

authority: anyone (the registry rotation path is the production caller)
reachability: Unrestricted view with one production consumer: the rotation facet redenominates a generation on it at `migrationMandateSpent` (RedemptionExt.sol:504), and only when the slice came from the primary leg. It returns true only when the guild budgeted at least one whole position `BPS_ONE` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:683) AND that budget has been spent out of the generation's own position `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:683), so secondary-leg slices counted in `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:708) can never declare a migration complete. Because slices take a share of CURRENT liquidity, a spent budget does not mean a drained position (DERIVED).

Reachable only from the immutable `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:698); the production call is the rotation facet booking a slice at `consume` (RedemptionExt.sol:437), AFTER the liquidity has moved, so a reverted slice burns no budget. The remainder from `allowance` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:700) is the liveness test and the bound: zero remaining or an oversized slice reverts `BadParam` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:707), which keeps `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:708) at or below maxTotalBps and both counters inside uint16 (DERIVED). The primary-leg share is booked separately at `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:709) — the caller asserts which leg it came from, this contract cannot check it (DERIVED) — and exhaustion stands the envelope down at `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:718) so it stops blocking `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:386). The counters are bps of a moving position, never token amounts, and nothing here verifies a balance.
observations: comment `Registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:690) says the function is registry-only; code `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:698) checks the registry but reverts with the guardian's error `NotGuardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:698).

comment `propose` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:711) cites the proposal gate at line 322 and comment `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:712) cites line 409; code puts that gate at `envelope` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:386) and declares `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:516).

reachability: Private, reached from `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:483) in execute, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:600) in the scan, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:611) in the executability test and `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:746) in the public view. Two conditions: a strict majority at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:725), so a tie fails, and a quorum of `QUORUM_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735) — ten percent — of the supply measured at the proposal's own `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735), not live, so minting or burning after the vote opens cannot move the bar. The comparison at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:736) is inclusive, and the division at `need` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735) truncates, so the effective quorum rounds DOWN (DERIVED).
observations: comment `vote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:729) says quorum is read at the same timepoint the vote weighs ballots and points at line 384; code weighs ballots at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:412) and reads the denominator at `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:735).

reachability: Private and unreferenced: no call site exists for `_settled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:739) anywhere in the file, so it is unreachable from every external entry and contributes no runtime behaviour (DERIVED). Had it been used it would report a proposal as settled once `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:741) or `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:741) is set or its window has closed — a WEAKER condition than `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:607) and a different one from `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:626).

Unrestricted view for interfaces: it answers whether `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:746) holds right now, with no timing test at all, so it reports on an open vote and on a long-stale one alike. An id that was never proposed reads false because both tallies are zero and the majority test at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:725) fails first (DERIVED).

Internal, reached from `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:370) when a target is named and again from `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:498) when the envelope is installed. Two exemptions make it a no-op: a native destination returns at `quote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:783) and an unset oracle returns at `o` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:785). Otherwise it calls out to the guardian-controlled `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:784) and treats a zero price as fatal `QuoteNotPriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:786); a reverting oracle propagates and blocks both proposing and executing, and a guardian able to repoint `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:791) therefore controls whether any non-native mandate can be installed (DERIVED).
observations: comment `setQuoteAllowed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:753) names the registry's allowlist setter; code in the registry declares it as `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:290) and writes the mapping at `allowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:303).

reachability: Only the current `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:792) may write `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:793), with no zero-check and no code-check, and it may be rewritten any number of times. Because the stored address is called during both `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:370) and `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:498), the holder of this setter can make any non-native quote unproposable and unexecutable, or clear the slot to skip the check entirely at `o` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:785) (DERIVED).
observations: comment `Timelock` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:789) says the oracle is timelock-set, and comment `timelock` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:48) says only the timelock adds assets; code gates this setter on `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:792) and the allowlist on the registry owner at `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:290).
